headline: Sam Altman said that treating AI models as a religious authority is a real safety issue, in a post widely read as a jab at Anthropic.
score_reason: A direct public statement by the head of OpenAI on a live dispute between the two leading labs; one outlet read in full, Axios blocked.
importance_line: The two most prominent AI labs now disagree in public about whether models deserve moral or spiritual standing, which shapes how their products talk to millions of users, though Altman named no one and Anthropic has not replied.
summary: OfficeChai reports, as did Axios, that OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman wrote on X on 3 Oct 2026 that he is "very uncomfortable" with people ascribing "religious force or a surrender of human judgment" to AI models and called it "a real safety issue". The post named no one, but it followed a New York Times report of 29 Sep that rival lab Anthropic has spent months consulting religious scholars about whether its Claude models might have moral status, a question Anthropic's own constitution calls "deeply uncertain".
notes: Axios original blocked (403); entry built from OfficeChai, which quotes the X post. Follow-up of 1003:C05-03 (Anthropic and the Vatican); new today is Altman's post.
